answers.10_unverifiable: Real-bet selection CLV (no verified recommendation links); real-bet entry spread; closing depth for CFB (top-of-book catalog proxies only), 30 of 36 NBA and 10 of 25 NHL fills (no archived book for the ticker), 64 NFL fills (no book in the close's run) and 24 NFL books observed after kickoff (excluded); limit-order behaviour for CFB, NBA, NHL, soccer, tennis, CBB, MLB (no tape); NFL weeks other than week 4; maker fee schedule per series; soccer (9 bets), tennis (0), CBB (no ledger), MLB (no executable-CLV code or ledger found).
answers.1_price_advantage_vs_closing_ask: Essentially zero. Executable purchase CLV (close ask - our fee-exclusive fill): NFL +0.02¢ (95% CI -0.11 to +0.14, n=170); CFB -0.02¢ (95% CI -0.20 to +0.17, n=59); NBA +0.10¢ (95% CI -0.59 to +0.65, n=36); NHL +0.31¢ (95% CI +0.06 to +0.58, n=25). In 56-69% of fills the executable price was exactly unchanged. Only NHL's interval excludes zero (n=25, 21 games; one of four comparisons, so not a finding).
answers.2_vs_previous_negative_midpoint: The previously reported midpoint CLV (NFL -0.60¢, CFB -0.55¢, NBA -0.74¢, NHL -0.59¢) is not a worse price than a closing buyer got: it equals the executable result minus the closing half-spread (NFL 0.62¢, CFB 0.53¢, NBA 0.83¢, NHL 0.90¢). Selling at the closing bid instead would have lost NFL -1.22¢, CFB -1.08¢, NBA -1.57¢, NHL -1.49¢.
answers.3_spread_vs_fees: Per contract versus the closing midpoint (cents): NFL price disadvantage -0.02 + closing half-spread 0.62 + exchange entry fee 1.69 = 2.28; CFB price disadvantage +0.02 + closing half-spread 0.53 + exchange entry fee 1.71 = 2.26; NBA price disadvantage -0.10 + closing half-spread 0.83 + exchange entry fee 1.72 = 2.46; NHL price disadvantage -0.31 + closing half-spread 0.90 + exchange entry fee 1.56 = 2.15. The exchange fee is 2-3x the spread cost and our price disadvantage versus a closing buyer is ~0; the entry spread itself is not observable for owner-placed fills and is not invented.
answers.4_positive_executable_clv: By sport only NHL has an interval above zero (+0.31¢, CI +0.06 to +0.58, n=25, 21 games): one of four sport comparisons, so not a finding by itself. By market family in real bets (cells with n>=8 fills; 12 cells across NFL, CFB, NBA) exactly one interval excludes zero: NBA spreads +0.60¢ (CI +0.10 to +1.40); it is a post-hoc subgroup of a 36-fill sport and should be treated as a flag to re-test, not an edge. NFL game-winner is borderline (lower bound 0.0). Hypothetical early-taker advantage over a closing buyer has an interval above zero for 2 of 41 NFL families (WINMARGIN, 1HFT) before any multiple-comparison control; the rest are indistinguishable from or worse than a closing buyer.
answers.5_would_early_limit_orders_improve_resul: Not demonstrably. When a resting order fills it does get a better price than the closing ask: +1.1 to +1.9¢ on the optimistic bound and 0 to +2.6¢ on the conservative bound (conservative intervals span zero). But many orders would not fill, and the pattern is consistent with adverse selection on the conservative bound: AT_BID fills see the midpoint drift against them by -0.2 to -1.0¢ (48h to 6h) while unfilled orders see it move away in our favour by +0.8 to +3.2¢ (the optimistic bound shows no such pattern). Early IMMEDIATE (taker) entry is worse than waiting: CYCLE -2.62c; T-24h -0.54c; T-6h -0.00c; T-90m +0.06c; T-30m +0.11c versus a closing buyer.
answers.6_fill_percentage: One week, 30 decisions, bounds not points. Full-fill rate of determinate orders, conservative to optimistic: AT_BID 33-55% (48h), 31-78% (24h), 43-68% (12h), 27-65% (6h), 5-69% (1h); one tick above the bid or inside the spread 38-83% (24h), 10-69% (1h). The conservative bound rests on 9-20 determinate orders per cell and is missing for 49 of 120 placements (no book). AT_ASK is 100% by construction (displayed size not tested).
answers.7_strongest_entry_window: None can be called. 12h-24h has the best combination of fill bounds and price improvement, but the conservative-bound intervals include zero everywhere and the sample is one week (16 games, 30 decisions). Not independently tested across weeks.
answers.8_repeatable_advantage_after_fees_fills_: No. Resting orders look better than buying at the close (-0.3 to +0.3¢ per decision versus -2.1¢) only because an unfilled bet is scored as zero, i.e. as not betting. Break-even edge: resting beats crossing at the close only if the bet's edge over the closing mid is below about 2.3-3.6¢ (conservative; interval to ~9¢) or 5.7-13.7¢ (optimistic). Observed selection drift is +0.37¢, so no strategy here shows an advantage after fees, fill probability and opportunity cost.
answers.9_changes_to_execution_research: (1) Record the entry quote and book at the moment of each real fill so spread and slippage can be separated. (2) Persist the recommendation-to-order link (digest refs) so selection CLV and execution CLV apply to the same bets. (3) Archive trade tape and order books for CFB, NBA and NHL; without them limit-order tests there are impossible. (4) Run the limit-order test across all NFL weeks with the tape, with maker/taker fee rules per series confirmed. (5) Evaluate entry windows as taker-vs-close comparisons first (cheap), limit orders second. (6) Never report ask-based or bid-based CLV without its midpoint and spread decomposition. (7) Add T-48h, T-12h and T-1h projection horizons.

metric_definitions.early_entry_taker_advantage: HYPOTHETICAL: closing ask - horizon ask on the model side. >0 means an immediate early taker paid less than a closing buyer. Equals selection CLV + (closing half-spread - entry half-spread): a widened closing spread inflates it without any change in fair value.
metric_definitions.executable_purchase_clv: closing ASK of the held side - our actual fee-exclusive fill VWAP (cents). >0: we paid LESS than someone buying at the close. 0: the executable price did not change. <0: waiting would have been cheaper. Never uses a bid as a purchase price.
metric_definitions.fee_adjusted: each measure minus the exchange-reported entry fee per contract, subtracted exactly once. A hypothetical liquidation also shows a MODELLED sale fee separately; a position held to settlement has no sale fee.
metric_definitions.limit_order_fill: HYPOTHETICAL: a resting buy fills only when the historical trade tape shows an aggressor selling that side into it. Reported as LOWER (back of queue, no cancellation credit) and UPPER (front of queue) bounds; 'uncertain' where evidence is missing; never assumed.
metric_definitions.liquidation_clv: closing BID of the held side - our actual fill VWAP (cents): what we could sell for at the close versus what we paid. Equals midpoint_execution_clv - closing half-spread.
metric_definitions.midpoint_execution_clv: closing midpoint - our actual fill VWAP (cents). The traditional mark-to-market measure; kept unchanged. Equals executable_purchase_clv - closing half-spread.
metric_definitions.size_adjusted_purchase_clv: depth-walked ask VWAP for OUR quantity at an archived closing order book minus our fill VWAP. Reported only where a same-ticker book observed before the start exists; otherwise unavailable, never approximated.

missing_evidence.real_bet_timing: most real fills are placed <1h before the start (NFL 138 of 170), so early-entry timing cannot be evaluated from real bets
